english: Let $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ be defined by $f(x)=\max\left\{\sin|x|,\ \cos|x|\right\}$. Let $S$ be the set of all $x\in[-2\pi,\pi]$ such that $f(x)=-\dfrac12$. If the sum of all elements of $S$ is $k\pi$, then the value of $k$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, $f(x)=\max\left\{\sin|x|,\ \cos|x|\right\}$ द्वारा परिभाषित है। माना कि $S$ उन सभी $x\in[-2\pi,\pi]$ का समुच्चय है जिनके लिए $f(x)=-\dfrac12$ है। यदि $S$ के सभी अवयवों का योग $k\pi$ है, तो $k$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $f(x)=g(|x|)$ with $g(t)=\max\{\sin t,\cos t\}$; for $t\in[0,2\pi]$: $g=\sin t$ on $\left[\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right]$, $g=\cos t$ otherwise
$t\in[0,\pi]$: $\sin t\ge0$, so $g(t)\ge0$; hence no $x\in[0,\pi]$ is in $S$

$x\in[-2\pi,0)$: $t=-x\in(0,2\pi]$. Line $y=-\frac12$ meets $g$ at $t=\frac{7\pi}{6}$ (sine branch, as $\frac{7\pi}{6}<\frac{5\pi}{4}$) and $t=\frac{4\pi}{3}$ (cosine branch, as $\frac{4\pi}{3}>\frac{5\pi}{4}$)
$t=\frac{11\pi}{6}$ ($\sin=-\frac12$) and $t=\frac{2\pi}{3}$ ($\cos=-\frac12$) are not points of $g=-\frac12$, since there the other function is larger
solution_full: Since $f$ depends on $|x|$, $f(x)=g(|x|)$ where $g(t)=\max\{\sin t,\cos t\}$; the graph of $f$ for $x<0$ is the mirror image of that of $g$ for $t>0$.

On $[0,2\pi]$, $\sin t\ge\cos t$ exactly on $\left[\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right]$. So $g(t)=\cos t$ on $\left[0,\frac{\pi}{4}\right]$, $g(t)=\sin t$ on $\left[\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right]$, and $g(t)=\cos t$ on $\left[\frac{5\pi}{4},2\pi\right]$.

The graph of $g$ falls from $1$ to $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$, rises to $1$ at $\frac{\pi}{2}$, falls to its least value $-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ at $\frac{5\pi}{4}$, then rises to $1$ at $2\pi$. As $-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}<-\frac12$, the line $y=-\frac12$ meets it twice in $[0,2\pi]$, once on each side of $\frac{5\pi}{4}$.

On the sine branch: $\sin t=-\frac12$, $t\in\left[\frac{\pi}{4},\frac{5\pi}{4}\right]\Rightarrow t=\frac{7\pi}{6}$. On the cosine branch: $\cos t=-\frac12$, $t\in\left[\frac{5\pi}{4},2\pi\right]\Rightarrow t=\frac{4\pi}{3}$.
The other roots of $\sin t=-\frac12$ and $\cos t=-\frac12$ ($t=\frac{11\pi}{6}$, $t=\frac{2\pi}{3}$) lie on the wrong branch: there $g=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$.
For $x\in[0,\pi]$, $t=x\in[0,\pi]$ gives $\sin t\ge0$, so $f(x)\ge0$: no solutions.
originality_note: New: the horizontal line y = -1/2 against the graph of max{sin|x|, cos|x|} on the asymmetric interval [-2pi, pi]; the level -1/2 lies between the minimum -1/sqrt2 and 0, so one root comes from each branch and only the left half of the interval contributes (way 5). Closest known: counting solutions of max(sin x, cos x) = 1/2 on (-2pi, 5pi) (ALLEN item). Different because: the |x| reflection, the negative level that cuts both branches near their junction, and a sum instead of a count.

concept_use.Number of solutions by graphical interse: The solutions are the intersections of y = -1/2 with the graph of f; the graph shows one meeting on each side of t = 5pi/4.
concept_use.Graphs of |f(x)|, f(|x|), |f(|x|)| and m: f(x) = g(|x|) is the mirror image of g = max{sin t, cos t}, whose branches switch at pi/4 and 5pi/4; this decides which roots are real points of the graph.
